artworks.title: Odysseus and Diomedes Capturing Dolon
artworks.description: The Lucanian red-figure vase that named its painter freezes Iliad Book X: Odysseus and Diomedes seize the Trojan spy in his wolf-skin as he prowls toward the Achaean ships. Dolon's night raid ends before it begins — the doomed volunteer of the Doloneia.

artworks.title: The Capture of Dolon (Ambrosian Iliad)
artworks.description: A miniature from the Ambrosian Iliad shows Odysseus and Diomedes taking Dolon at night — late antique book art preserving the Homeric ambush in gold and pigment. The spy's wolf-skin mission becomes a page of illuminated disaster. Biblioteca Ambrosiana, Milan.

artworks.title: Dolon
artworks.description: Preller's Romantic reading isolates the Trojan spy in his animal disguise — the wolf-clad scout of Book X caught between courage and folly. Nineteenth-century myth illustration keeps Dolon as the night's most expendable volunteer.

artworks.title: Terracotta Figurine of Dolon
artworks.description: A small terracotta from the Staatliche Antikensammlungen presents Dolon in his wolf-skin kit — the Homeric spy reduced to a handheld figure of night and disguise. Even in clay, the Doloneia's doomed scout keeps his animal camouflage. Munich.

popCulture.title: Doloneia
popCulture.description: Iliad Book 10 takes its scholarly name from Dolon — the wolf-skin spy whose capture opens the night raid that kills Rhesus.

popCulture.title: Rhesus
popCulture.description: The Attic Rhesus keeps Dolon as the volunteer scout in wolf-skin — Hector's spy whose mission ends before the Thracian king falls.

popCulture.title: Dolon
popCulture.description: The Trojan spy in the wolf-skin remains the night raid's doomed volunteer — caught, questioned, and killed before Rhesus falls.
